label: conj:dispersion-suppression-scale
title: Archimedean suppression of the substrate $q$-dispersion below the gamma-ray-burst bounds
html:
Conjecture. Archimedean suppression of the substrate q-dispersion below the gamma-ray-burst bounds

At the fibre level, a mode of wavenumber k on a one-dimensional channel (channel) advances with the q-integer phase [k]_q. Its group velocity carries fractional corrections of order \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} relative to the substrate light speed c_q = 1/(q-1) (information speed of light).

Conjecture. The archimedean projection suppresses the fibre-level q-dispersion. The residual fractional variation of the archimedean photon group velocity with photon energy \mathfrak{E} is bounded by \mathfrak{E} / \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{QG}} for a suppression scale \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{QG}} at or above the Planck energy.

This bound is required for compatibility with the gamma-ray-burst time-of-flight limit [abdo2009]. The observational context and the relation to doubly-special-relativity phenomenology appear in the DSR remark. The framework derives the fibre-level deformation but does not yet specify the mechanism by which the substrate-to-archimedean projection removes the O(\hbar_q) residue from macroscopic propagation.
